codes.construct: Mystical experience (MEQ-30) and semantic similarity of LLM-generated psychedelic narratives
codes.texts: 3,000 LLM-generated psychedelic trip narratives; 1,085 human Erowid trip reports (used only as a similarity reference)
codes.models: Gemini 2.5, Claude Sonnet 3.5, ChatGPT-5, Llama-2 70B, Falcon 40B (the same model completes the MEQ-30 on its own narrative)
codes.human_reference: None. Humans did not code or rate any units. Erowid reports serve only as an embedding-similarity corpus.
codes.note: The LLMs generate the narratives and self-rate them on the MEQ-30. No human coder applied the MEQ-30 to the same units, and no LLM–human agreement statistic is reported. The only correlation reported is between the two LLM-derived metrics (Pearson r = 0.661), which is not an agreement statistic against a human reference.

codes.construct: Diagnosis of schizophrenia spectrum disorders from two clinical vignettes
codes.texts: Two simulated clinical vignettes (David, Michael) of schizophrenia spectrum disorders
codes.models: DeepSeek-V3, Llama 3.1 405B, Mixtral-8x22B, Phi-3.5-mini, Ministral-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Haiku, Gemini Flash 1.5
codes.human_reference: None; LLM diagnoses were compared with the vignettes' known correct diagnosis and with the published accuracy of psychiatrists (33% got both right)
codes.note: Research letter. It tests LLM diagnostic accuracy on 2 vignettes against the known diagnosis (a criterion). Humans did not code the same units with the LLM. It reports no unit-level agreement statistics.

codes.construct: Empathy and emotion/intent recognition quality of LLM responses to synthetic user statements (PASS and WIN scores)
codes.texts: LLM-generated (GPT-4) synthetic user statements (10,000 across 5 life scenarios) and responses from 11 LLMs; 1000 responses per task rated by humans
codes.models: GPT-4 as automatic judge (0/1 PASS and WIN); evaluated LLMs include Claude2, LLaMA2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, BLOOM, Falcon, Vicuna
codes.human_reference: Three volunteer female graduate students in psychology scored responses with the same PASS/WIN metrics
codes.human_human_agreement: Krippendorff's alpha was computed, and ratings below 0.7 were discarded and replaced. No value is reported.

agreement_stats.configuration: Automatic vs human scores, normalized to a 1-100 scale, across LLMs
agreement_stats.quote: The Pearson correlation coefficient achieves 0.991, indicating a strong alignment.

codes.note: Mainly a benchmark of LLMs as responders, but GPT-4 also judges response empathy and is compared with humans. The r=0.991 is computed on per-model aggregates (about 12 points, Fig. 6), not per unit, so I5 is borderline. Table 6 is emotion classification accuracy against dataset labels.

codes.construct: Well-being/functioning (GAF-derived 1-10 score) and adaptive vs maladaptive self-state evidence (MIND framework) in social media posts
codes.texts: Social media timelines (posts) from the CLPsych 2025 shared task, with annotated evidence spans and well-being scores
codes.models: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B (LoRA) for evidence identification and well-being rating; Qwen2.5-32B ICL for summaries; baselines zero-shot Llama 3.1-8B, BART-Large, BERT
codes.human_reference: Shared-task annotations of adaptive/maladaptive evidence spans and well-being scores (annotators not described in this paper)

agreement_stats.configuration: Task A.2 well-being rating, macro F1 over impairment classes
Task A.2 well-being rating, macro F1 over impairment classes
Task A.1 evidence identification, overall recall (span-level, BERTScore recall)

codes.note: CLPsych 2025 shared-task system paper. Metrics (macro F1, MSE, BERTScore recall) are against gold annotations; annotators and unit counts not described. Well-being MSE: 2.01 (class.) and 2.17 (gen.). Summary tasks use NLI consistency, not human agreement. Borderline: annotation procedure not described.

codes.construct: Psychiatric diagnosis of DSM-5-TR clinical cases and DSM knowledge multiple-choice questions
codes.texts: 21 DSM-5-TR clinical case vignettes and 95 multiple-choice self-exam questions (published textbook material)
codes.human_reference: No human coding of the texts. The reference is the textbook answer key. 11 psychiatry residents were comparators, not the reference.
codes.note: Letter. LLMs and residents were both scored against the textbook answer key (GPT-4 diagnosis F1 63.41%, knowledge accuracy 85.05%). This is a benchmark of correct answers, not agreement with human coders of the same units. It is also largely a knowledge exam task. No LLM-human agreement statistic is reported. The Jaccard similarity between residents and GPT-4 is not agreement on a coding scheme.

codes.construct: DSM-5-TR psychiatric diagnosis from case vignettes
codes.texts: 93 DSM-5-TR Clinical Cases vignettes (55 test set)
codes.models: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o (base prompting vs decision-tree prompting)
codes.human_reference: Author-designated diagnoses from the casebook (not independent human coders applying a scheme)
codes.note: The LLMs predict diagnoses. The reference is the casebook author's diagnosis, which works as an external diagnostic criterion, not human coding. PPV, sensitivity and F1 are reported. The paper has no human-coder comparison arm. Borderline: a reviewer could treat it as a benchmark.

codes.construct: Quality of LLM-generated behavioral treatment goals rated on SDT and Goal Setting Theory dimensions (autonomy, competence, clarity, etc.)
codes.texts: GPT-3-generated behavioral goals for two outcome goals (not patient or clinical texts being coded)
codes.models: GPT-3 (generator of goals, not a rater)
codes.human_reference: 8 students rated the LLM-generated goals on 5-point Likert scales
codes.note: Prototype and feasibility study. Humans rate GPT-3 outputs, and the LLM does not rate or code any units. No LLM-human agreement statistic is reported.

codes.construct: Utterance-level emotion labels in conversations (IEMOCAP, MELD, EmoryNLP)
codes.texts: Dialogue utterances from acted conversations and TV-show dialogues (IEMOCAP, MELD, EmoryNLP)
codes.models: Fine-tuned (LoRA) ChatGLM, ChatGLM2, Llama, Llama2 (7B); zero-shot ChatGPT3.5
codes.human_reference: Benchmark gold emotion labels. The annotator details are in an appendix that isn't in the text.
codes.note: General NLP emotion-recognition benchmark (weighted F1 against dataset gold labels). The texts are acted or TV dialogue, not clinical. Whether humans annotated the labels isn't stated in the text we received, and the dataset appendix is missing. A reviewer should decide on I2 and the label provenance; E3 is possible.

codes.construct: Quality of ChatGPT (GPT-4) relationship-therapy responses (empathy, reflection, validation, therapeutic questioning)
codes.texts: 20 single-session ChatGPT relationship-advice conversations and user interviews
codes.models: GPT-4 / ChatGPT (as the object being evaluated, not as a rater)
codes.human_reference: Two authors coded the chatbot sessions on 21 codes; users were interviewed
codes.note: Humans (the authors) rate ChatGPT outputs. No LLM rates the same units, so ChatGPT is the object and not the rater. The user-vs-author agreement percentages are human-human, not LLM-human.

codes.construct: Depression, stress, interpersonal risk factors (perceived burdensomeness/thwarted belongingness), wellness dimensions, and stress causes in social media posts (IMHI benchmark)
codes.texts: Reddit/SMS social-media posts from the IMHI benchmark (DR, Dreaddit, Irf, MultiWD, SAD); test sets of 405 to 2,441 posts
codes.models: MentalQLM (Qwen1.5-0.5B, dual LoRA), ChatGPT zero-shot and few-shot, GPT-4 few-shot, MentalLlama-7B, MentalLlama-chat-7B, MentalLlama-chat-13B, Qwen1.5/Qwen2 variants
codes.human_reference: Human-annotated labels of the IMHI benchmark datasets (DR, Dreaddit, Irf, MultiWD, SAD). The paper does not say who annotated them.

agreement_stats.configuration: dual LoRA instruction-tuned, weighted F1, mean over 5 datasets

codes.note: Model-development paper that reports weighted F1 against the human-annotated IMHI labels. The paper does not say who produced the labels, so check whether they come from annotators or from self-reports and metadata. GPT-4o judging of reasoning quality has no human comparison. No human-human agreement is reported.

codes.construct: Analytic thinking (thinking style) scores from ChatGPT versus LIWC dictionary-based analytic thinking index
codes.texts: arXiv abstracts, UK petitions, Yelp reviews, death row last statements (about 16,000 texts); also participant writing samples from prior work
codes.models: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) and GPT-4 via the OpenAI API, three prompts (general, specific, formula)
codes.human_reference: None. The reference is the LIWC dictionary score. No human coders applied the scheme to the texts.
codes.note: The reference is the LIWC dictionary tool, not human coders. The authors list comparisons to human ratings as future work. The need-for-cognition analysis uses an external questionnaire criterion. The exclusion could also be coded E2 or E5.

codes.construct: Stress, depression severity, suicide ideation and C-SSRS suicide risk level in Reddit/Twitter/SMS posts
codes.texts: Social media posts (Reddit, Twitter, SMS-like messages) from Dreaddit, DepSeverity, SDCNL, CSSRS-Suicide, Red-Sam, Twt-60Users, SAD datasets with human annotations
codes.models: Alpaca 7B, Alpaca-LoRA, FLAN-T5 XXL, LLaMA2 70B, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 (zero-shot, few-shot); finetuned Mental-Alpaca and Mental-FLAN-T5
codes.human_reference: Human annotations in the source datasets (multiple annotators for Dreaddit, 2 for DepSeverity, 4 psychiatrists for CSSRS-Suicide, 2 experts for Red-Sam, 2 for Twt-60Users, manual labels for SDCNL)

agreement_stats.configuration: instruction finetuned, Task #5 binary suicide risk

codes.possible_duplicate: None known; this is the arXiv version (2307.14385v4) of the IMWUT 2024 article.
codes.note: Only balanced accuracy against human-annotated labels is reported (fits I5). Main task is T3; Tasks 1, 2 and 4 are binary presence labels (closer to T1). Labels are consensus labels from the source datasets. Tables 4, 9 and 10 give more models and tasks than listed here.

codes.construct: Reflective design practices and self-regulated learning (SRL) in think-aloud utterances during brainstorming with ChatGPT
codes.texts: Think-aloud transcripts from 17 designers (about 88 utterances each) and their design sketches
codes.models: ChatGPT 3.5 was the tool participants used. It did not code or rate anything.
codes.human_reference: Human researchers coded the utterances and two human coders scored the sketches.
codes.human_human_agreement: Cohen's kappa between two human coders per code in Table 1, ranging from 0.74 to 1. Sketch rubric: same scores 90% of the time on 29% of the sketches.
codes.note: ChatGPT was the object of study, not a rater. All coding was done by humans, so there is no LLM–human agreement statistic.

codes.construct: Educational short-answer grading (rubric indicators) and transparency of LLM scoring architecture; not a psychological or clinical construct
codes.texts: 10 synthetic student short-answer responses, 3 rubric indicators
codes.models: Unspecified LLM in single-agent vs multi-agent architectures (900 Monte Carlo runs)
codes.human_reference: None; no human raters. The authors list human-rater benchmarking as future work.
codes.note: The study is about educational grading and architectural transparency. The only ICC is for repeated-run reliability of the LLM (multi-agent ICC(1,k)=0.9921), not LLM–human agreement. There is no human coding and the construct is not psychological.

codes.construct: Mental health risk in multi-turn conversations (safe vs self-harm vs harm-to-others), detected by a safety classifier plus an LLM pass-gate. Secondary: clinicians rate escalation appropriateness and rapport of chatbot replies (T4-like, humans rate only).
codes.texts: 662 synthetic multi-turn LLM–patient-simulator transcripts (9,348 turns) grounded in CRADLE Bench Reddit narratives. External checks used NVIDIA Aegis 2.0 prompts and CRADLE Bench posts.
codes.models: The architecture combines a 4B context-aware safety classifier (Farinhas et al.; probably a fine-tuned decoder LLM, not confirmed in the text) with a GPT-5-chat reasoning pass-gate. The conversational LLMs were GPT-5-chat and Qwen3.5-27B.
codes.human_reference: Five doctoral-level licensed US clinical psychologists labelled each turn for risk. A conversation counted as at risk if at least one annotator flagged any turn (conservative reference).
codes.human_human_agreement: Conversation level: Krippendorff's alpha 0.79, Gwet's AC1 0.80. Turn level: alpha 0.60, AC1 0.88.

agreement_stats.configuration: Conversation-level risk detection, overall, safety layer ON
agreement_stats.quote: overall specificity of 0.85 (95% CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.88;0.95), and F1 score of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89;0.94)
sensitivity was 0.88 (95% CI: 0.81; 0.93), specificity 0.94 (95% CI: 0.90; 0.97), and F1 score 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84; 0.93)
sensitivity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.82; 0.92), a specificity of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.96; 0.99), and an F1 score of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.90; 0.95)

codes.note: Borderline on I3: the rater is a 4B classifier plus a GPT-5-chat pass-gate; the text does not say the 4B model is a decoder LLM. Statistics are sensitivity, specificity and F1, not kappa. Turn-level results are in Supplementary Table 3 (not provided). Reference label is a union of annotators.

codes.construct: Documented goals-of-care discussions in EHR clinical notes (palliative care process measure)
codes.texts: EHR progress notes of hospitalized seriously ill adults (University of Washington trials, 2018-2023)
codes.human_reference: Manual chart abstraction by abstractors (consensus); Trial 2 used BERT-screened human abstraction

agreement_stats.configuration: Trial 2 held-out test set, note-level, max F1

codes.note: The construct is a clinical documentation or process measure (palliative care communication), not a mental state or psychological treatment process. I judged it outside I2. The reviewer may reconsider: the LLM was compared with human labels (F1, AUC). Trial 2 human labels were partly BERT-screened.

codes.construct: Emotion regulation modes (individual ER per Gross PMER, co-regulation, socially shared regulation) in chatbot messages
codes.texts: GPT-4 chatbot (GroupBuddy) messages in Discord group channels; coded subset is 10% of n=75 messages
codes.models: ChatGPT o1 (prompted with codebook) as second coder
codes.human_reference: One human researcher independently coded the same 10% subset

agreement_stats.configuration: Codebook prompt, after two refinement iterations, 10% subset vs human researcher
agreement_stats.quote: It took two iterations of refining the codebook and the prompt to achieve a satisfactory level of agreement (κ = 0.85)

codes.note: Weak fit: the units are chatbot (helper) responses, and the construct is ER strategies in an educational setting. The kappa is on a small subset and was obtained after prompt refinement on that same subset. Humans and the LLM applied the same codebook, so it is borderline eligible. The reviewer should check the construct and the refinement iterations.
